synopsis: UL 4600, third edition dated 17 March 2023, structures an autonomous-product safety case around questions and claims answered with evidence, rather than prescribed designs, tests or performance numbers [f12261, f15375, f12262, f15377]. Its coverage includes hazards, operating domain, perception, machine learning, metrics and field feedback, with conformance judged by the completeness of the responses [f12263]. The booklet recommends borrowing those question lists for the heavy off-road collision-mitigation validation plan and suggests 1.5–3 pages for the safety scope and top-level claim, using GSN v3 and UL 4600 as sources [f9984, f10156]. However, an automatic brake on an operator-driven machine is not an autonomous product, no off-road body has adopted UL 4600, and the plan should borrow its thoroughness without claiming compliance [f12267, f12269, f12270]. These recommendations do not establish simulation acceptance: the research did not examine UL 4600's simulation-credibility content or verify its simulation-acceptance provisions, and it also records both proponents and critics of safety cases [f7706, f15383, f10319].
